title: New Lord of the Rings Movie Is Still on Its Way
summary:
Fans of The Lord of the Rings can relax. A new movie co-created by TV host Stephen Colbert is still being developed, despite rumors this weekend that it had been put on hold, Polygon reports.

On October 4, a website called Knight Edge Media reported that the project was "paused" because two big entertainment companies, Paramount and Warner Bros., have merged. But the report did not name a specific source. On October 5, Rob Keyes of the website Screen Rant called the report "inaccurate." He wrote that the movie's status was "exactly as it was weeks ago," with writers still working and no budget or filming date confirmed yet. Warner Bros. also contacted Knight Edge Media to say the movie is "not 'canceled' and is still in development."

The film, tentatively called The Lord of the Rings: Shadows of the Past, was announced in March 2026 by Peter Jackson, who directed the original Lord of the Rings movies. Colbert, a famous fan of author J.R.R. Tolkien, is working on it with his son, screenwriter Peter McGee, and with Philippa Boyens, who helped write the earlier films.

The story will take place 14 years after Frodo has passed on. His hobbit friends Sam, Merry and Pippin set out to retrace the first steps of their old adventure. Meanwhile, Sam's daughter, Elanor, discovers a long-buried secret about the War of the Ring. The movie will draw on early chapters of the first book that were left out of the original films.

Fans will not have to wait for it to visit Middle-earth again. Another movie, The Hunt for Gollum, directed by Andy Serkis, is set to reach theaters on December 17, 2027.
why_it_matters: It shows how a rumor can spread online and why checking sources and official statements matters.
